name: Badami Cave Temples
description: Carved out of red sandstone cliffs between the 6th and 8th centuries by the Early Chalukyas, a complex of four magnificent rock-cut cave temples dedicated to Shiva (Cave 1), Vishnu (Caves 2 & 3), and Jain Tirthankaras (Cave 4), overlooking the emerald Agastya Lake and Bhutanatha Temples.

name: 100 Feet Road Indiranagar
description: One of India's most celebrated cosmopolitan lifestyle streets, stretching from Old Airport Road to CMH Road, packed with artisanal microbreweries, gourmet eateries, and designer flagship stores.

name: Ashoka Pillar Monument Jayanagar
description: Inaugurated on August 20, 1948 by the last Maharaja of Mysore Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar, a 30-foot stone pillar bearing the four-lion capital marking the founding of Jayanagar.

name: Avalahalli State Forest
description: A preserved eucalyptus, acacia, and scrub reserve forest in north Bangalore offering off-road mountain biking trails, dirt tracks, and quiet forest birding.

name: Bannerghatta National Park
description: A 260-square-kilometer national park established in 1974 on the southern fringes of Bangalore, featuring a tiger and lion safari, India's first butterfly conservatory, and elephant corridors.

name: Bengaluru Fort
description: Originally constructed as a mud fort in 1537 by Kempe Gowda I and converted into a formidable stone fortress in 1761 by Hyder Ali, surviving the British siege of 1791.

name: Bengaluru Palace
description: Built in 1878 by Chamarajendra Wadiyar X inspired by England's Windsor Castle, featuring Tudor-revival architecture, fortified towers, battlements, stained glass, and hunting trophies.

name: Brahmin's Coffee Bar Bangalore
description: Founded in 1965 in Shankarapuram, a legendary tiny standing-room breakfast joint renowned across India for feather-soft idlis, crunchy uddin vadas, and fresh coconut chutney.

name: Brigade Road Shopping Bangalore
description: A high-energy retail corridor connecting MG Road to Residency Road, buzzing with international footwear outlets, denim stores, music shops, and historic pubs.

name: Bugle Rock Park
description: A historic 3,000-million-year-old Peninsular Gneiss rock formation where Kempe Gowda I erected one of the four original watchtowers marking Bangalore's city boundaries in the 16th century.

name: Church Street Bengaluru
description: A vibrant 750-meter cobblestone pedestrian avenue lined with legendary independent secondhand bookstores (Blossom, Bookworm), artisan cafes, indie music bars, and street art.

name: Commercial Street Bengaluru
description: One of Bangalore's oldest and most energetic shopping streets, packed with hundreds of boutiques selling bridal lehengas, imitation jewelry, fabrics, Pashmina shawls, and footwear.

name: Conrad Bengaluru
description: A soaring 24-storey luxury hotel overlooking the scenic Ulsoor Lake, featuring Tiamo Mediterranean poolside dining, Mikusu Asian gastronomy, and a rooftop cocktail lounge.

name: CSI St. Mark's Cathedral Bangalore
description: Consecrated in 1816, an elegant colonial church inspired by St. Paul's Cathedral in London, featuring roman arches, a grand dome, and a serene leafy compound on MG Road.

name: Cubbon Park
description: A sprawling 300-acre green lung created in 1870 by Major General Richard Sankey, housing over 6,000 indigenous and exotic trees, the Seshadri Iyer Memorial Hall, and scenic shaded avenues.

name: Diamond District Bangalore
description: One of Bangalore's landmark early IT and residential campuses built along the Old Airport Road, representing the dawn of India's Silicon Valley boom in the 1990s.

name: Dodda Basavana Gudi (Bull Temple)
description: Built in 1537 by Kempe Gowda I in Dravidian style, housing one of the world's largest monolithic Nandi bulls, carved out of single granite rock measuring 15 feet high and 20 feet long.

name: Freedom Park Bengaluru
description: Formerly the Central Jail of Bangalore built in 1867 where political leaders were detained during the Emergency, converted into a 21-acre public cultural park, museum, and amphitheater.

name: Gandhi Bhavan Museum Bangalore
description: Established in 1965 on the picturesque shores of the historic Kumara Krupa grounds, displaying rare photographs, letters, spinning wheels, and archival publications on Mahatma Gandhi.

name: HAL Heritage Centre and Aerospace Museum
description: India's first aerospace museum established in 2001 by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, showcasing historic aircraft like the Marut, Kiran, MiG-21, Canberra, and flight simulators.

name: IIM Bangalore Campus (Indian Institute of Management)
description: Spread over 100 lush green acres on Bannerghatta Road, designed by legendary Pritzker Prize laureate B.V. Doshi, featuring stone-pergola corridors, open courtyards, and deep integration with nature.

name: IISc Bangalore Heritage Campus
description: Founded in 1909 through the visionary partnership of Jamsetji Tata and Maharaja Krishnaraja Wadiyar IV, a 400-acre academic forest campus featuring the iconic neo-classical Main Building and clock tower.

name: ISKCON Temple Bangalore
description: Perched atop Hare Krishna Hill, one of the world's largest ISKCON temple complexes, consecrated in 1997 with a 56-foot gilded dhwaja-stambha, stunning chandeliers, and Vedic cultural halls.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru Planetarium and Indira Gandhi Park
description: Established in 1989 by Bangalore City Corporation, housing a 15-meter hybrid projection dome that displays immersive astronomy shows, accompanied by an open-air Science Park.

name: Jayamahal Garden
description: A leafy neighborhood park tucked into the historic Jayamahal royal palace precinct, featuring walking pathways, stone benches, and blooming flowering shrubs.

name: Jayaprakash Narayan Biodiversity Park (JP Park)
description: A 85-acre eco-park in north Bangalore featuring three freshwater lakes, indigenous tree plantations, a musical fountain, and specialized bamboo and medicinal gardens.

name: Kanaka Sarovar Lake
description: A quiet freshwater lake surrounded by walking tracks and wetlands near Kalyan Nagar, home to local and migratory waterbirds.

name: Koshy's Restaurant & Parade Cafe
description: Operating on St. Mark's Road since 1940, a cherished colonial-era restaurant where prime ministers, writers, artists, and journalists gather for mutton cutlets, stew, and appams.

name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
description: A 240-acre historic garden commissioned by Hyder Ali in 1760 and completed by Tipu Sultan, featuring over 1,850 plant species, centuries-old trees, and the iconic London Crystal Palace-inspired Glass House.

name: Lalbagh Peninsular Gneiss Rock
description: A prominent granite hillock inside Lalbagh designated as a National Geological Monument, dating back 3,000 million years to the Archean epoch with a Kempe Gowda watchtower on top.

name: Lalbagh Waterfall and Lake
description: The scenic southern water body inside Lalbagh Botanical Garden featuring an artificial waterfall, lotus ponds, and a bird refuge hosting spot-billed pelicans and purple moorhens.

name: Lumbini Gardens and Nagavara Lake
description: A public recreational eco-friendly waterfront park on the shores of Nagavara Lake along the Outer Ring Road, featuring pedestrian tracks, paddle boating, and amusement rides.

name: M. Chinnaswamy Stadium
description: Established in 1969 with a 40,000 seating capacity, home of Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB) and world-renowned for being the first solar-powered international cricket ground with a SubAir drainage system.

name: MG Road Bangalore (Mahatma Gandhi Road)
description: The historic central commercial boulevard of Bangalore developed during the British Cantonment era, today lined with international fashion stores, silk emporiums, and metro stations.

name: MN Krishna Rao Park
description: A 25-acre heritage park established in 1940 named after Dewan M.N. Krishna Rao, shaded by mature canopies of rain trees, tabebuias, and gulmohar.

name: MTR Restaurant (Mavalli Tiffin Room)
description: Founded in 1924 near Lalbagh, the historic inventor of Rava Idli during WWII wheat rations, famous for pure silver-service thalis and ghee-dripping masala dosas.

name: Muthyala Maduvu Waterfall (Pearl Valley)
description: A serene waterfall cascading down a 92-meter rock face nestled in a deep valley near Anekal, where thin cascading water droplets resemble strings of pearls ('Muthu').

name: National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA Bengaluru)
description: Housed in the restored 3.5-acre heritage Manikyavelu Mansion surrounded by century-old trees and mirror pools, displaying modern Indian art by Raja Ravi Varma, Jamini Roy, and Amrita Sher-Gil.

name: NIMHANS Convention Centre
description: An elite academic, scientific, and cultural convention center situated on the lush NIMHANS campus, hosting major medical conferences, national symposia, and cultural events.

name: Radisson Blu Atria Bengaluru
description: A centrally located hotel on Palace Road near Golf Course, featuring the signature One Atrium dining restaurant and Tea & Wine lounge.

name: Residency Road Bangalore
description: A historic artery in the heart of the Bangalore Cantonment, lined with premier heritage institutions (St. Joseph's), upscale hotels, handicraft emporiums, and iconic pubs.

name: St. Mary's Basilica Shivajinagar
description: Built in 1882, the oldest church in Bengaluru and the only church in Karnataka elevated to the status of a minor basilica, renowned for exquisite stained glass windows and annual St. Mary's Feast.

name: Taj MG Road Bengaluru
description: A prestigious luxury hotel on MG Road celebrated for signature dining experiences including Chinese fine dining at Memories of China and North Indian cuisine at Trinity Square.

name: The Leela Palace Bengaluru
description: A palatial luxury hotel inspired by the royal architectural grandeur of the Vijayanagara Empire and Mysore Palace, set in 7 acres of landscaped gardens with copper domes and brass sculptures.

name: The Oberoi Bengaluru
description: A premier luxury hotel built around a magnificent 120-year-old rain tree, renowned for landscaped tropical water gardens, and award-winning dining at Rim Naam and Polo Club.

name: The Park Hotel Bangalore
description: A vibrant boutique hotel designed by Conran & Partners featuring Italian restaurant Italia, 24-hour eatery Monsoon, and the chic poolside lounge bar Aqua.

name: Tipu Sultan Summer Palace
description: Constructed entirely out of French-influenced teakwood between 1781 and 1791 within the Bengaluru Fort complex, featuring intricately carved pillars, fluted arches, and floral balconies.

name: UB City Mall & Dining Bengaluru
description: India's first luxury shopping mall spanning 1.6 million square feet with four architectural towers, housing flagship global luxury boutiques (Louis Vuitton, Rolex) and open-air amphitheater restaurants.

name: Vidhana Soudha Bengaluru
description: Built in 1956 under Chief Minister Kengal Hanumanthaiah, the imposing seat of the state legislature of Karnataka showcasing magnificent Neo-Dravidian granite architecture.

name: Visvesvaraya Industrial & Technological Museum
description: Established in 1965 in honor of Bharat Ratna Sir M. Visvesvaraya, featuring 7 interactive galleries spanning engine mechanics, aerospace, biotechnology, electro-technics, and space science.

name: Barid Shahi Tombs Bidar
description: A sprawling 55-acre heritage garden park containing the monumental domed tombs of the Barid Shahi rulers who governed the Bidar Sultanate from 1487 to 1619.

name: Bidar Fort
description: Built in 1427 when Sultan Ahmad Shah Wali moved the Bahmani capital to Bidar, featuring 10 kilometers of red laterite ramparts, triple-layer defensive rock-cut moats, and the Rangin Mahal.

name: Bandipur National Park
description: An 874-square-kilometer national park established in 1974 under Project Tiger, forming a crucial part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve along the Karnataka-Tamil Nadu border.

name: Bharachukki Waterfalls
description: The wider, curving eastern branch of the Shivanasamudra Falls where the Kaveri cascades across a 250-meter rocky amphitheater resembling Niagara Falls.

name: Kemmangundi
description: Kemmangundi, located in the Tarikere taluk of Chikmagalur district, is a breathtaking hill station in Karnataka. With a rich history dating back to the 16th century, Kemmangundi was a favorite summer retreat of Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, the king of Mysore. The region is known for its stunning natural beauty, with the Western Ghats range surrounding it. The hills are covered with lush green forests, and the area is home to a variety of flora and fauna, making it a nature lover's paradise. Visitors can trek through the hills, go bird watching, take leisurely nature walks, and capture the stunning scenery through photography. The region has a pleasant climate throughout the year, making it an ideal destination for those seeking a peaceful getaway from the hustle and bustle of city life.

name: Kudremukh Peak & National Park
description: Spanning 600 square kilometers across the Western Ghats, named after its distinct mountain peak shaped like a horse's face ('Kudre-mukh' in Kannada) rising to 6,214 feet (1,892 m), world-famous for rolling emerald shola grasslands and wild Bengal tigers.

name: Mullayanagiri Peak Chikmagalur
description: Rising 6,317 feet (1,925 m) above sea level in the Chandra Drona hill range of the Western Ghats, the highest mountain summit in Karnataka, crowned by a small temple dedicated to Tapasvi Mullappa Swamy and offering sweeping 360-degree views of coffee estate valleys.

name: Panambur Beach Mangalore
description: Recognized as one of the cleanest and safest beaches in coastal Karnataka, operated with professional lifeguards, offering jet skiing, parasailing, camel rides, and hosting the prestigious biennial International Kite Festival.

name: Hoysaleswara Temple Halebidu
description: Inscribed as an UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023, a 12th-century masterpiece of Hoysala architecture built on a star-shaped platform, featuring two identical shrines dedicated to Hoysaleswara and Santaleswara with thousands of intricate relief sculptures depicting epics, celestial maidens, and wildlife friezes.

name: Gulbarga Fort and Great Mosque
description: Originally built by Raja Gulchand of the Kakatiyas and strengthened in 1347 by Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah, housing the unique Spanish Cordoba-inspired Jama Masjid with 68 domed bays.

name: Abbey Falls Coorg
description: Located 8 km from Madikeri, where numerous mountain streams unite to plunge 70 feet down a vertical rock face into a frothing pool, accessible via a private coffee and spice plantation walk and viewed from a hanging pedestrian bridge.

name: Brindavan Gardens Mysore
description: Laid out in 1932 beneath the massive Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) dam across the Kaveri River, spanning 60 acres of symmetrical terraces, illuminated fountains, and music-synchronized water shows.

name: Cauvery Split Katte (Shivanasamudra River Confluence)
description: The serene point where the holy Kaveri River splits into twin branches encircling the sacred island of Shivanasamudra, forming the Gaganachukki and Bharachukki cascades.

name: Colonel Bailey's Dungeon
description: An underground vaulted brick dungeon below the river ramparts where Tipu Sultan held British prisoners of war (including Colonel Bailey, who died here in 1782) chained to stone slabs.

name: Daria Daulat Bagh (Tipu Sultan Summer Palace)
description: Built in 1784 set amidst manicured Mughal-style gardens, an exquisite teakwood summer palace renowned for wall-to-wall canvas murals depicting the Battle of Pollilur (1780).

name: Gaganachukki Waterfalls
description: A thunderous 98-meter segmented waterfall where the Kaveri River plunges off the Deccan Plateau through a deep rocky gorge into a foaming emerald pool.

name: Melukote
description: Melukote, situated in the Mandya district of Karnataka, is a tranquil hill town that boasts a rich history, cultural significance, and breathtaking natural beauty. This ancient town is home to the famous Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple, a prominent pilgrimage site, and the Yoganarasimha Temple, which attracts devotees and architecture enthusiasts alike. The town's stunning landscape, with its lush green forests, rolling hills, and scenic valleys, offers a perfect setting for nature walks, photography, and bird watching. With its unique blend of history, culture, and natural beauty, Melukote is an ideal destination for those seeking a peaceful retreat from the hustle and bustle of city life.

name: Mysore Lotus Pond Srirangapatna
description: A serene historic stone water pond in Srirangapatna blooming with pink and white sacred lotus blossoms, surrounded by flowering trees.

name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
description: Formed in 1648 when a weir was built across the sacred Kaveri River, an internationally recognized Ramsar wetland site comprising six riverine islets that serve as a crucial breeding ground for painted storks, spoonbills, and black-headed ibises alongside resident mugger crocodiles.

name: Shivanasamudra Falls
description: Shivanasamudra Falls, located in the Mandya district of Karnataka, is a breathtaking waterfall that attracts visitors from all over the world. The falls are surrounded by lush green forests, steep rocks, and rolling hills, creating a picturesque landscape that is perfect for nature lovers and adventure seekers. The waterfall is formed by the Kaveri River, which splits into two branches, creating two separate falls, the Gaganachukki and the Bharachukki. The falls are surrounded by a variety of flora and fauna, making it a great spot for bird watching and nature photography. The best time to visit Shivanasamudra Falls is during the monsoon season, when the water level is at its peak and the surrounding landscape is lush and green.

name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple Srirangapatna
description: Consecrated in 984 CE by the Western Ganga dynasty and expanded by Hoysalas and Vijayanagara kings, one of the five sacred 'Pancharanga Kshetrams' dedicated to Lord Vishnu reclining on Adisesha.

name: Srirangapatna Breach Commemorative Obelisk
description: A historic granite obelisk monument marking the exact breach in the fortress walls where British forces stormed Srirangapatna on May 4, 1799, and where Tipu Sultan was slain.

name: Srirangapatna Fort and Tipu Sultan Palace Ruins
description: The historic citadel built in 1454 by Timmanna Hebbar and fortified by French engineers for Tipu Sultan, featuring triple-layer stone moats, subterranean dungeons, and Lal Mahal palace foundations.

name: Srirangapatna Historic Island Town
description: An egg-shaped island in the Kaveri River that served as the de facto capital of Mysore under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, steeped in Hoysala, Vijayanagara, and Sultanate history.

name: Srirangapatna Jama Masjid (Masjid-i-Ala)
description: Constructed in 1782 by Tipu Sultan, an imposing mosque featuring two soaring octagonal minarets with pigeonholes, clock faces, and 98 steps ascending to panoramic island views.

name: Tipu Sultan Museum Daria Daulat Bagh
description: Housed on the upper floor of Daria Daulat Bagh, displaying authentic oil paintings, Sir Eyre Coote portraits, Persian decrees, Tipu Sultan's personal clothes, swords, and war medals.

name: Tipu Sultan Resting Place (Gumbaz Srirangapatna)
description: Built in 1784 by Tipu Sultan as a mausoleum for his parents and later for himself, set within a Persian-style garden with 36 polished black hornblende pillars, ebony doors inlaid with ivory, and a grand dome.

name: Chennakeshava Swamy Temple Somanathapura
description: Consecrated in 1268 CE by Soma, a general under Hoysala King Narasimha III, an UNESCO-inscribed star-shaped trikuta temple exhibiting the apex of Hoysala stone relief carving.

name: Devaraja Market (Mysore City Centre Market)
description: Established during the reign of Chamarajendra Wadiyar IX in the late 19th century, a bustling 3-acre heritage market packed with over 800 stalls of fragrant Mysore jasmine, kumkum pyramids, and betel leaves.

name: Mysore Boating Karanji Lake
description: A 90-acre scenic lake at the base of Chamundi Hills, home to India's largest walk-through aviary, a butterfly park, and pedal boating on tranquil waters.

name: Mysore Chamundeshwari Temple
description: Perched at 3,300 feet atop Chamundi Hills, an ancient 12th-century temple dedicated to Goddess Chamundeshwari (Durga), featuring a grand 7-tier gopuram built by the Maharaja of Mysore.

name: Mysore Chikka Gadiyara Market (Dufferin Clock Tower)
description: The historic 1886 ornate Victorian clock tower erected in honor of Viceroy Lord Dufferin, marking the northern entrance to the vibrant Devaraja Market.

name: Mysore Jaganmohan Palace and Art Gallery
description: Completed in 1861 as an alternate royal residence, home to one of South India's richest art museums showcasing original oil paintings by Raja Ravi Varma, including 'Glow of Hope'.

name: Mysore Mahadevpura Shooting Spot - Coconut Park
description: A tranquil coconut palm plantation situated along the meandering Kaveri River near Mahadevapura, famous as an idyllic backdrop for scores of South Indian movies.

name: Mysore Mahishasura Statue
description: The brightly painted colossal statue of the demon Mahishasura holding a sword and snake, erected in 1659 by Dodda Devaraja Wadiyar atop Chamundi Hill.

name: Mysore Nandi Statue
description: Carved in 1659 out of a single black basalt granite outcrop on the 700th step of Chamundi Hill, one of India's largest monolithic Nandi bulls measuring 16 feet tall and 24 feet long.

name: Mysore Palace (Amba Vilas Palace)
description: Designed by British architect Henry Irwin and completed in 1912, the official residence of the Wadiyar dynasty showcasing Indo-Saracenic grandeur, stained glass domes, ivory doors, and golden thrones.

name: Mysore Railway Museum
description: Established in 1979 by Indian Railways, India's second oldest railway museum displaying the 1899 Maharani's Saloon dining carriage, vintage steam locomotives, and an operating mini-train.

name: Mysore Shukavana Bird Park
description: An internationally acclaimed walk-through aviary holding the Guinness World Record for the most bird species in an aviary (over 460 species), established by Sri Ganapathy Sachchidananda Swamiji.

name: Mysore Sunset Point Chamundi Hill
description: A scenic roadside mountain overlook perched halfway down Chamundi Hills, offering sweeping panoramic views of Mysore Palace, Lalitha Mahal, and Karanji Lake.

name: Mysore Zam Zam Bazar
description: A lively traditional shopping bazaar near St. Philomena's Cathedral known for Mysore silk sarees, sandalwood perfumes, attar oils, and local Muslim street delicacies.

name: Mysore Zoo (Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens)
description: Established in 1892 by Maharaja Chamarajendra Wadiyar, one of the oldest, most beautifully landscaped zoos in the world, spanning 157 acres housing gorillas, giraffes, white tigers, and elephants.

name: St. Philomena's Cathedral Mysore
description: Constructed in 1936 under Maharaja Nalvadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar inspired by Germany's Cologne Cathedral, one of Asia's tallest churches with soaring 175-foot twin spires.

name: Talakkadu Panchalinga Temples
description: An enigmatic historic town on the banks of the Kaveri River where over 30 ancient temples dating from the Ganga, Chola, and Hoysala dynasties remain buried beneath shifting sand dunes.

name: BLR-MYS Highway Hillpoint View (Ramadevara Betta)
description: A dramatic granite outcrop at Ramanagara along the Bengaluru-Mysuru corridor, famed as India's only dedicated Long-billed Vulture Sanctuary and the iconic filming location for the movie 'Sholay'.

name: Wonderla Amusement Park Bangalore
description: India's top-rated amusement and water theme park spanning 82 acres on Mysore Road, featuring over 60 high-thrill roller coasters, reverse loops, wave pools, and water slides.

name: Honnemardu
description: Honnemardu, a quaint town in the Shimoga district of Karnataka, is nestled in the Western Ghats mountain range. The town is surrounded by lush green forests, rolling hills, and the tranquil backwaters of the Linganamakki dam, creating a picturesque landscape that is perfect for nature lovers and adventure seekers. With its rich biodiversity, Honnemardu is a haven for bird watchers, with over 200 species of birds documented in the area. The region's unique geography and climate also make it an ideal destination for trekking, kayaking, and other outdoor activities. As the sun sets over the backwaters, the sky is painted with hues of orange and pink, making Honnemardu a photographer's paradise.

name: Agumbe Rainforest & Barkana Falls
description: Known as the 'Cherrapunji of the South', one of the wettest places in India receiving over 7,000 mm of annual rainfall, home to dense virgin rainforests, the Agumbe Rainforest Research Station (ARRS) studying wild King Cobras, Barkana Falls (850 ft), and sunset viewpoints over the Arabian Sea.

name: Jog Falls Shivamogga
description: Plunging 253 meters (830 ft) in a thunderous sheer drop down rugged Western Ghats cliffs on the Sharavathi River, formed by four distinct roaring cascades named Raja, Roarer, Rocket, and Rani.

name: Devarayanadurga
description: The shaded natural perennial spring emerging from a solid rock fissure, flanked by deciduous forest tracks and ancient deer sanctuaries.

name: Madhugiri Monolith
description: The Madhugiri Monolith, a 3930 feet tall monolithic granite hill, is a trekker's paradise in the Tumkur district of Karnataka. This gigantic rock structure, one of the largest in Asia, has been a focal point of historical and cultural significance. The hill is surrounded by the remains of the Gopalakrishna temple and the Madhugiri Fort, which date back to the 17th century, offering a glimpse into the region's rich history. As visitors ascend the monolith, they are rewarded with breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape, making it an ideal destination for adventure seekers, nature lovers, and those seeking a spiritual connection with the great outdoors.

name: Maravanthe Beach & Coastal Highway
description: One of India's most scenic coastal stretches along National Highway 66, where the highway runs along a narrow natural strip with the roaring waves of the Arabian Sea on one side and the calm freshwater Souparnika River on the other.

name: Banavasi
description: Banavasi, nestled in the Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka, is a treasure trove of ancient history, spiritual significance, and cultural richness. This quaint village is often referred to as the 'first capital' of ancient Karnataka, with its roots dating back to the Kadamba dynasty. The village is home to the revered Madhukeshwara Temple, a 9th-century shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, which attracts devotees and history enthusiasts alike. As you wander through the village, you'll discover a plethora of ancient temples, each with its unique architectural style and historical significance, making Banavasi an ideal destination for those seeking a spiritual and culturally enriching experience. The village's tranquil atmosphere, surrounded by lush green forests and rolling hills, also provides an ideal setting for meditation, yoga, and photography, allowing visitors to reconnect with nature and their inner selves.

name: Dandeli
description: Dandeli, situated in the Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka, is a haven for adventure seekers and nature lovers. With its dense forests, teeming with wildlife, and the Kali River flowing gently through it, Dandeli offers an unforgettable experience. The region is known for its rich biodiversity, and the Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary, which is home to animals like the black panther, elephant, and bison. The sanctuary is also a bird watcher's delight, with over 200 species of birds, including the rare hornbill. Visitors can explore the forest's depths by trekking through its numerous trails, which offer breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape.

name: Gokarna
description: A working pilgrimage town with a string of crescent beaches strung along cliffs to the south. The vibe is barefoot, slow and unmistakably Indian — chai shacks, fishing boats and rocks lit copper at sunset.

name: Karwar Beach
description: Karwar Beach, situated in the Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka, is a tranquil getaway nestled between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea. This picturesque beach town offers a unique blend of natural beauty, rich history, and cultural significance. With its stunning coastline, scenic islands, and historical landmarks, Karwar Beach is an ideal destination for those seeking to escape the chaos of city life and connect with nature. The beach is lined with casuarina trees, and its shoreline is dotted with rocky outcrops, making it a perfect spot for swimming, sunbathing, and leisurely walks.

name: Murudeshwar Temple & Raja Gopura
description: Situated on Kanduka Hill surrounded on three sides by the Arabian Sea, featuring the world's second-tallest Shiva statue soaring 123 feet (37 m) and an astounding 20-storey high Raja Gopura (249 ft) equipped with high-speed passenger elevators.

name: Yana Rocks
description: Yana Rocks, nestled in the Sahyadri mountain range of Karnataka, is a breathtaking destination known for its unique limestone formations and lush green forests. The site is home to two massive monolithic rocks, Bhairaveshwara and Mohiniyattam, which are not only a marvel of nature but also hold significant spiritual and cultural importance. As visitors wander through the forests surrounding Yana, they can immerse themselves in the serene beauty of nature, observe the rich biodiversity of the region, and catch glimpses of the local wildlife, making it an ideal spot for those who seek to connect with nature and experience the authentic charm of rural Karnataka.

name: Hampi Group of Monuments
description: Sprawling over 4,100 hectares amidst surreal boulder-strewn hills along the Tungabhadra River, the UNESCO World Heritage capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, featuring the iconic Stone Chariot at Vijaya Vittala Temple, Virupaksha Temple, Lotus Mahal, and Elephant Stables.

name: Gol Gumbaz Vijayapura (Bijapur)
description: Completed in 1656 as the mausoleum of Sultan Mohammed Adil Shah, featuring the second-largest unsupported dome in the world (44 meters external diameter) constructed without pillars, world-famous for its Whispering Gallery.

name: Malliabad Fort & Elephant Troughs
description: The 13th-century Kakatiya stone fortress ruins featuring massive limestone blocks, ancient step-wells, and monolithic stone horse mangers.

name: Jaladurga Fort Gorge
description: A medieval river fortress perched atop an island hillock where the Krishna River forces itself through a dramatic, narrow rocky canyon.

name: Gabbur (The Temple Village)
description: An open-air museum village housing over 30 ruined Chalukyan and Kalyani-era stone temples and carved step-wells hidden among modern farmhouses.

name: Revana Siddheshwara Betta (SRS Hills)
description: A single colossal monolithic granite hill rising sharply from the plains, featuring ancient cave temples and a rugged stone stair climb.

name: Kanva Dam Backwaters (Fishermen's Edge)
description: The quiet, unpaved northern banks of the Kanva reservoir, far from the main dam bund, popular for waterbird watching and calm waters.

name: Savandurga Rear Forest Trails (Karigudda Base)
description: The quiet deciduous forest trails wrapping around the base of one of the largest single-rock monoliths in Asia.

name: Mekedatu Sangama Southern River Bed
description: The quiet, sandy granite shelves downstream from the Arkavathi-Cauvery confluence, where the river carves deep chutes through solid granite.

name: Gajanur Tunga Dam Backwater Coves
description: Calm, forest-fringed reservoir arms located upstream from the main dam, offering uncrowded water viewpoints and quiet morning mist.

name: Channagiri Fort
description: An 18th-century hilltop stone fortification offering unbroken 360-degree views of the surrounding agrarian plains and hill ranges.

name: Bhadra Reservoir (Lakkavalli Edge)
description: The quiet, non-commercial peripheral dikes along the Bhadra Tiger Reserve buffer zone, ideal for seeing river terns and forest margins.

name: Madhugiri Monolith Rear Ascent Trails
description: The unpaved boulder slopes and ancient ruined granaries along the flanks of Asia's second-largest monolithic rock hill.

name: Borokanave Reservoir
description: The oldest modern irrigation project in the district (built in 1892), nestled in a dramatic rocky gap in the Suvarnamukhi river basin.

name: Barkur Royal Alleys & Chaulikeri Tanks
description: The medieval capital of the Alupa dynasty, filled with ancient ruined stone temples, coastal step-wells, and traditional tile-roofed homesteads.

name: Mattu Beach & Sea-Plankton Shallows
description: A quiet coastal strip lined with coconut palms and black-sand edges, known for seasonal night bioluminescence and traditional vegetable farming.

name: Anegudde Foot-Trails & River Estuaries
description: The quiet mangrove creeks and backwater canals weaving behind the coastal headlands near Kumbhashi.

name: Mirjan Fort Inner Moats & Hidden Well Rooms
description: An overgrown 16th-century laterite fort associated with Queen Chennabhairadevi (the "Pepper Queen"), featuring interconnected stone cisterns and high circular bastions.

name: Gullapur & Aghanashini Estuary Buffers
description: The untouched mangrove channels and tidal mudflats where the unpolluted Aghanashini River enters the sea, home to traditional bivalve shell harvesters.

name: Shirve High Mountain Meadow (Ankola)
description: A hidden high-elevation plateau overlooking the Arabian Sea coastline, accessed via off-road tracks through evergreen forests.

name: Ainapur (Bara Kaman Outer Tombs)
description: The unfinished 12-arched stone mausoleum of Ali Adil Shah II, alongside the quieter suburban ruins of the Afzal Khan palace and step-tank.

name: Torvi Subterranean Aqueducts (Sangeet Mahal)
description: The ruins of Nauraspur, an ancient twin city housing the arched Sangeet Mahal and an engineered underground water-channel network.

name: Kumatgi Royal Pleasure Pavilions
description: A rural outpost built by the Adil Shahis featuring medieval cooling pavilions, copper-pipe water fountains, and wall paintings depicting European visitors.

name: Kamalapuram Historic Lake Bunds
description: An ancient 14th-century irrigation reservoir built by the Vijayanagara rulers, surrounded by stone aqueducts and quiet banana groves away from the Hampi monuments.

name: Sandur Forest Valleys & Narihalla Dam
description: An emerald, iron-rich mountain bowl featuring the Narihalla reservoir gorge, cool ghat passes, and pine-clad hills.

name: Kudligi Megalithic Cairns
description: Ancient stone circles and prehistoric cairn burials scattered across the granite boulder plains of southern Vijayanagara.

name: Hampi Anegundi River Crossings
description: The less-traveled, peaceful northern bank of the Tungabhadra River, featuring prehistoric rock art shelters, the Pampa Sarovar, and coracle river paths.

name: Wankanagari Fort Ruins
description: An ancient stone citadel tucked inside rural scrub hills, featuring massive rough-hewn stone gates and ruined watchtowers.

name: Shorapur (Surpur) Taylor's Manzil & Royal Fort
description: The 19th-century colonial hill bungalow of British resident Meadows Taylor, offering sweeping vistas of the historic Surpur battlements and town.

name: Yadgir Fort Hillock & Ancient Water Cisterns
description: A natural boulder fortress towering over the plains, housing rock-carved defensive structures, cannons, and medieval rainwater-harvesting pools.

name: Bhima-Krishna Confluence (Near Tintini)
